title: Sizing and scaling ACI and Container Apps
learningObjective: Give containers the right CPU and memory. Set up Container Apps scale rules, including scale to zero. Remember that ACI doesn't autoscale.
foundation: Each container needs a certain amount of CPU and memory, which you set when you deploy it.
Azure Container Instances runs exactly what you deploy and does not add copies by itself.
Azure Container Apps adds and removes copies (replicas) automatically based on rules such as HTTP traffic, and can go down to zero when idle.
engineer: ACI sizing: set CPU and memory per container. The group's total must fit the region's limits. GPUs work in some regions.
Changing ACI size: you can't change a running group. Redeploy with new values.
Scaling out ACI: create more container groups yourself (for example behind Application Gateway), or use Container Apps or AKS instead.

Container Apps sizing: on the Consumption plan, CPU and memory come in fixed pairs, from 0.25 vCPU with 0.5 GiB up to 4 vCPU with 8 GiB. Memory is always 2 × vCPU. Workload profiles (dedicated) allow bigger sizes.
Replicas: set a minimum and maximum number of copies (replicas) per revision. The minimum can be 0. The maximum is 10 by default and can be raised.
Scale rule types: HTTP, by concurrent requests per replica (default 10); TCP, by concurrent connections; CPU or memory use; custom KEDA scalers, for example by Azure Service Bus queue length.
Scale to zero: with minimum replicas 0, an idle app costs nothing for compute. The catch: the first request after idle is slow (cold start).
How scaling works: decisions are made per revision. The scaler (KEDA) checks the event source and adds replicas, up to the maximum. For APIs that must answer fast, set the minimum to 1 or more.

example.title: A worker that follows the queue
body: An order-processing worker on Container Apps uses a Service Bus scale rule: one replica for every 20 messages, minimum 0, maximum 30. Overnight it scales to zero. At peak it reaches 30 replicas.
An old report job stays on ACI with 2 vCPU and 4 GiB. A Logic App starts it when needed.

prerequisites: Something to scale on (HTTP ingress, a queue, and so on)
limits: ACI: no autoscale; size is fixed per deployment
Container Apps Consumption: fixed CPU and memory pairs
portal: Container App > Scale: min/max replicas and scale rules (HTTP, TCP, custom).
ACI: redeploy with new CPU/memory values.
configuration.cli:
az containerapp update -g rg-app -n api --cpu 0.5 --memory 1.0Gi --min-replicas 1 --max-replicas 20 \
  --scale-rule-name http-rule --scale-rule-type http --scale-rule-http-concurrency 50
az container create -g rg-app -n aci-report --image mcr.microsoft.com/azuredocs/aci-helloworld --os-type Linux --cpu 2 --memory 4
configuration.powershell:
Update-AzContainerApp -ResourceGroupName rg-app -Name api -ScaleMinReplica 1 -ScaleMaxReplica 20
$c = New-AzContainerInstanceObject -Name report -Image mcr.microsoft.com/azuredocs/aci-helloworld -RequestCpu 2 -RequestMemoryInGb 4
New-AzContainerGroup -ResourceGroupName rg-app -Name aci-report -Location westeurope -Container $c -OsType Linux

lab.objective: Size containers and configure scaling for idle and peak load.
steps: Run with 250 concurrent requests and max 10 replicas; read the cap warning.
Switch to ACI under load and read why it cannot scale.

validation.text: Scaled a container app to zero

lab.cost: None. The simulation runs entirely in the browser.

troubleshooting.symptom: The container app is slow on the first request each morning.
troubleshooting.cause: It scaled to zero overnight (cold start).

troubleshooting.symptom: Requests queue up at peak time.
troubleshooting.fix: Raise the maximum, or the requests each replica can handle.

troubleshooting.cause: The Consumption plan needs fixed pairs.
troubleshooting.fix: Use a valid pair, or a dedicated workload profile.

comparisons.difference: Container Apps uses KEDA inside, without showing you the cluster.
ECS services on Fargate scale with Application Auto Scaling. App Runner scales by concurrent requests.

misconceptions.myth: Scale to zero deletes the app.
misconceptions.reality: No. Revisions stay. Replicas start again when work arrives.

misconceptions.myth: ACI can scale with rules, like a scale set (VMSS).

architectureDecisions: Pick the rule by workload: HTTP concurrency for APIs, queue or event rules for workers.
No cold starts allowed: keep minimum replicas at 1 or more.

walkthrough.subtitle: Give containers the right CPU and memory, and let Container Apps scale them for you.
learn: Replicas, scale to zero and revisions

steps.label: Sizing
steps.title: How big, and how many?
body: Too little CPU and the app is slow; too much and you overpay. And traffic changes during the day.

steps.label: ACI size
steps.title: ACI: you set the size, it stays
body: In ACI you request CPU and memory per container; the group's total is the sum. To change it, you redeploy. ACI has no built-in autoscale; for more copies, create more groups.

callout.text: Need automatic scaling for containers without managing Kubernetes? Choose Container Apps, not ACI.

steps.label: Rules
steps.title: Container Apps: scale rules
body: Each container app has minimum and maximum replicas and scale rules: HTTP (concurrent requests), TCP, CPU or memory, or event-driven rules from KEDA (for example queue length).

steps.label: Replicas
steps.title: Replicas grow, shrink and can reach zero
body: With minimum replicas 0, an idle app scales to zero and costs nothing for compute. CPU and memory per container are set in fixed combinations (for example 0.5 vCPU / 1 GiB).
Changes to the template create a new revision; you can split traffic between revisions.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Container scaling
body: ACI: fixed size. Container Apps: rules and replicas.
recap: ACI: CPU and memory per container; redeploy to change
Container Apps: HTTP, TCP, CPU/memory or KEDA rules

handsOn.title: Create a container app with an HTTP scale rule
handsOn.cost: Free or cents. Container Apps (Consumption) includes a monthly free grant; the app scales to zero when idle.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
If rg-az104-lab does not exist yet: search 'Resource groups' > Create > name rg-az104-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.

steps.do: Search 'Container Apps' > + Create > Container App. Group rg-az104-lab, name ca-lab, region your region, create a new Container Apps environment (Consumption only).
Container tab: tick 'Use quickstart image' (Simple hello world container).
steps.see: Defaults of 0.5 CPU and 1 GiB memory.

steps.do: Ingress tab: enable ingress, traffic from anywhere, target port 80. Review + create > Create.
steps.see: Deployment completes in a few minutes.

steps.do: Open ca-lab > Overview and browse to the Application Url.
Open Application > Scale (or Revisions and replicas > Edit and deploy > Scale). Set min replicas 0, max 5. Add a rule: HTTP scaling, concurrent requests 10. Create the new revision.
steps.see: A new revision with the scale rule.
The revision list and how many replicas are running. With no traffic it drops to 0 after a few minutes.

check: ca-lab has min 0, max 5 replicas and an HTTP rule.
cleanup: When you finish for the day: Resource groups > rg-az104-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete. This removes everything inside it.
